title: Intermediate financial reporting: IFRS and US GAAP
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Apply the conceptual framework and the main standards for revenue, receivables, inventories, property and intangibles, impairment, leases, income taxes, pensions, financial instruments, provisions, equity and earnings per share, and compare IFRS with US GAAP.
primary_reading: IFRS Foundation: IFRS Accounting Standards navigator (free to read)

weeks.1: The conceptual framework and standard setters
weeks.5: Property, plant and equipment and intangibles
weeks.11: Equity, share-based pay and earnings per share

blocks.deliverable: Compare an IFRS and a US GAAP income statement.
Apply the five-step revenue model to three contracts.
Test an asset for impairment under both frameworks.
Week 7 midterm; record a lease from both sides.
Compute a deferred tax asset and liability.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Reporting comparison: take one IFRS reporter and one US GAAP reporter in the same industry, identify five accounting policy differences in their notes, restate one key ratio on a comparable basis, and write a three-page memo on how the differences affect analysis.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
